sanskrit: namo nālayate śuṇḍāṃ viṣāṇena mṛṇāline | pratyakkamalakandāya karṇābhyāṃ parṇaśāline
close_translation: Homage to the one who with his trunk fondles the lotus-stalk, who wears the leaf by his ears — to the inner lotus-root: [homage] to Gaṇeśa.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: jayatyamūlamamlānamauttaraṃ tattvamadvayam | spandāspandaparispandamakarandamahotpalam
close_translation: Triumphs the rootless, unwilting, supreme, non-dual principle — the great lotus whose nectar is the trembling and the untrembling and the all-trembling (spanda-aspanda-parispanda).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kāruṇyāmṛtasindhoruditamivāvartamīkṣaṇāpāṅgāt | mauktikamayaṃ dadhānā tāṭaṅkaṃ jayati gauravī mūrtiḥ
close_translation: May the weighty form (gauravī mūrtiḥ) triumph — bearing, as it were, the pearl-made earring arisen from the whirlpool of the compassion-nectar-ocean, from the corner of [her] glance.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sphūrtaye viśvaśilpasya śrīśivānandamūrtaye | nityonmeṣanimeṣāyai nistuṣāyai namastviṣe
close_translation: Homage to the radiance (tviṣe) that is the blessed Śivānanda-form, for the flashing-forth of the world's craft — the ever-opening-and-closing, the chaffless (nistuṣā).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yasmādanuttaramahāhradamajjanaṃ me saubhāgyaśāmbhavasukhānubhavaśca yasmāt | tatsvātmacitkramavimarśamayaṃ gurūṇā-mavalliyugmamuditoditavīryamīḍe
close_translation: From which [comes] my immersion in the unsurpassed great pool, and from which the auspicious Śāmbhava-joy's experience — that pair of the gurus' feet, its power risen and arisen, made of the self-conscious order-of-reflection (svātma-cit-krama-vimarśa) — I praise.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: namo nikhilamālinyavilāpanapaṭīyase | mahāprakāśapādābjaparāgaparamāṇave
close_translation: Homage to the one skilled in dissolving all stain — to the supreme atom of the pollen of the great-prakāśa's lotus-feet.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: gorakṣo lokadhiyā deśikadṛṣṭyā maheśvarānandaḥ | unmīlayāmi parimalamantargrāhyaṃ mahārthamañjaryām
close_translation: I, Maheśvarānanda — a Gorakṣa in the world's view, in the deśika's vision — open the Parimala, the inner-apprehendable [commentary] on the Mahārthamañjarī.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: svakriyāyā api vyākhyāṃ svayameva prayuñjmahe | uparyapyātmasaṃrambhasambhogāmreḍanotsukāḥ
close_translation: Even for my own work I myself provide the commentary — above [the verse], eager for the repetition of the enjoyment of my own fervor.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yadvā vineyajanacittacamatkriyārtha-matrodyamo'yamudito'stu tadetadāstām | saṃkṣepavistaravibhāgaviviktaśobhaḥ puṣpāñjalirbhavatu vāṅmaya eṣa śambhoḥ
close_translation: Or rather — for the wonder of the minds of the teachable people, may this endeavor arise; let that be. May this verbal handful-of-flowers of Śambhu, adorned with the division into brief-and-extended, be [accepted].
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: avagataśivadṛṣṭipratyabhijñārthatattva-kramasaraṇirahasyollāsasarvasvavedī | gurucaraṇasaparyācāturīcidghano'haṃ gahanamapi hṛdantarvyoma tad vyākaromi
close_translation: I who know the whole secret-springing-essence of the Krama-path's truth — [having] understood the meaning of the Śivadṛṣṭi and the Pratyabhijñā — I, dense in the skill of serving the guru's feet, unfold even the dense inner-sky of the heart.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: iha mahati rahasyonmīlane maṅgalāya prabhavati mama saṃvidyoginīnāṃ prasādaḥ | api tu kulasaparyābimbasaṃbandhyavandhyāḥ sakṛdapi matimanto nainamudghāṭayantu
close_translation: Here, at the great opening of the secret, for the auspicious [rite] the grace of my awareness-yoginīs prevails; but the intelligent ones — barren through their connection with the reflection of the kula-worship — let them not open this, even once.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: svapnasamayopalabdhā sā sumukhī siddhayoginī devī | gāthābhiḥ saptatyā svāpitabhāṣābhirastu samprītā
close_translation: That fair-faced goddess, the siddha-yoginī, obtained at the time of a dream — may she be well-pleased with the seventy gāthās in her own-awakened speech.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vardhatāṃ deśikaḥ śrīmān saṃvinmārgaśca vardhatām | māheśvarāśca vardhantāṃ vardhatāṃ ca maheśvaraḥ
close_translation: May the blessed deśika flourish; may the path of awareness flourish; may the Māheśvaras flourish; and may Maheśvara flourish.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: paryAlochanavimukhe vastusvabhAvasyAtmano hR^idaye | sha~NkAviShavegeneva saMsArabhayena muhyati lokaH
close_translation: The world, in the heart of the self — whose object-nature is [normally] turned from examination — is bewildered by the fear of saṃsāra, as by the poison of doubt.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mANikyapraveka iva nicholito nijamayUkhalekhayA | pratibhAti laukikAnAmatyantasphuTo.apyasphuTa AtmA
close_translation: Like a peerless ruby wrapped in its own filaments of light: the self appears to the worldly as utterly-manifest-yet-unmanifest.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: Urdhvo jvalati prakAsho lokAlokasya ma~NgalapradIpaH | vimarshadashAmukhAnItadahyamAnamalAlitailavichChardaH
close_translation: Upward blazes the prakāśa — the lamp of auspiciousness of the world-and-non-world — its malāli-oil's flow drawn through the ten-reflexions' mouth, burning. [variant: "by the ten-reflexions' mouth the malāli-oil's flow is burnt"]
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sannaiva hR^idayaprakAsho bhavanakriyAyA bhavati kartA | saiva kriyAvimarshaH svasthA kShubhitA cha vishvavistAraH
close_translation: The heart-prakāśa, being, becomes the doer of the becoming-action; that same [awareness], the action-reflexion — at rest, the world's expansion [when] stirred.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: pR^ithvIparamashivayoH pratyAhAre prakAshaparamArthe | yo.anyonyavisheShaH sa eva hR^idayasya vimarshonmeShaH
close_translation: In the withdrawal of the earth and the supreme-Śiva, in the prakāśa's supreme-meaning: that which is the mutual distinction is itself the heart's reflexion-upsurge (vimarśa-unmeṣa).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tathA tathA dR^ishyamAnAnAM shaktisahasrANAmekasa~NghaTTaH | nijahR^idayodyamarUpo bhavati shivo nAma paramasvachChandaH
close_translation: Thus, of the thousands of powers as they are seen, the single-collision: becoming the form of one's own heart's effort — that is called Śiva, the supreme free (parama-svacchanda).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sa eva vishvamIkShituM sthAtuM kartuM chonmukho bhavan | shaktisvabhAvaH kathito hR^idayatrikoNamadhumAsalollAsaH
close_translation: He himself, becoming intent to see the world, to stand, to act — the power-natured, is declared the surge of the honey in the heart's triangle.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: j~nAnaM kriyeti dvayorapi prathamonmeShe sadAshivo devaH | dvitIyAyA ullekhe dvitIyaH sa bhavatIshvaro nAma
close_translation: Knowledge and action — in the first-upsurge of the two, the god is Sadāśiva; in the second's tracing (ullekha), he becomes the second, named Īśvara.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: j~nAtA sa AtmA j~neyasvabhAvashcha lokavyavahAraH | ekarasAM saMsR^iShTi yatra gatau sA khalu nistuShA vidyA
close_translation: He is the knower, the self; the world-transaction is of the known's nature; where the going is the one-taste's creation — that indeed is the huskless vidyā.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ekarase svabhAve udbhAvayantI vikalpashilpAni | mAyeti lokapateH paramasvatantrasya mohanI shaktiH
close_translation: In the one-taste nature, causing the crafts of the alternatives to arise — she is called māyā, the deluding power of the world-lord, the supremely free.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sarvakaraH sarvaj~naH pUrNo nityo.asa~Nkuchitashcha | viparIta iva mahesho yAbhistA bhavanti pa~nchashaktayaH
close_translation: The all-doer, the all-knower, the full, the eternal, the unshrinking — the great Lord, as it were inverted: by which [powers] those five powers come to be.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kallolAyamAnAni sadA hR^idayAmbunidhau trINi karaNAni | AkarShantIdantAM tatrAhantAM (tathA ahantAM) chAtrArpayanti
close_translation: The three instruments (karaṇas), ever waving in the heart-ocean, draw the "this"-ness and there offer the "I"-ness. [variant: "and the I-ness"]
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: hR^idayasthitasya vibhorviShayAloko vishR^i~Nkhalo bhavati | j~nAnendriyadIpeShu nijanijagolAgranityalagneShu
close_translation: For the lord dwelling in the heart, the object-light becomes unchained, in the knowledge-sense-lamps ever-attached to their own spheres' tips.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: bhavanti karaNAni pa~ncha khalu karmapradhAnAni lokanAthasya | spandate svaira yairjano jaDAdvilakShaNo bhavan
close_translation: The five instruments, indeed, are the action-principals of the world-lord, by which, moving freely, the person, becoming distinct from the inert, pulses (spanda).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vishvodyAnavirUDhAni gandhapramukhAni sugandhIni puShpANi | pa~nchApyAjighran krIDati trailokyadhUrto devaH
close_translation: The five fragrant flowers grown in the world's garden — smell and the rest — sniffing them all, the trickster-of-the-three-worlds god plays.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: styAnasya kramavashAdikShurasasyeva shivaprakAshasya | guDapiNDA iva pa~nchApi bhUtAni madhuratAM na mu~nchanti
close_translation: By the order of the thickening (styāna), like the sugar-cane-juice's: the five elements, like lumps of raw sugar [in the syrup], do not lose their sweetness — [so] of the Śiva-prakāśa.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sarvasya bhuvanavibhramayantrollAsasya tantuvallIva | vimarshasaMrambhamayI ujjR^imbhate shambhormahAshaktiH
close_translation: Like a creeper-thread [through pearls] of all the worlds' whirling upsurge: the reflexion-fervor-natured great-power of Śambhu unfolds (ujjṛmbhate).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yadadhvanAM cha ShaTkaM tatra prakAshArthalakShaNamardham | vimarshashabdasvabhAvamardhamiti shivasya yAmalollAsaH
close_translation: The six of the courses (adhvans): there the half is of the prakāśa-meaning's mark; the half of the reflexion-word's nature — such is Śiva's yāmala-upsurge.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: AlekhyavisheSha iva gajavR^iShabhayordvayaH pratibhAsaH | ekasminnevArthe shivashaktivibhAgakalpanAM kurmaH
close_translation: Like the appearance of the elephant-and-bull in a painting: in the single object we make the Śiva-Śakti division's imagining.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tilamAtre.api sharIre prekShadhvaM kITasyaitAvatI shaktiH | sA svachChandashriyo vishvasharIrasya kiyatI bhavatu
close_translation: In a body of mere sesame's size — look! — such is the power of the worm: how great must it be of the world-body, the fortune of the free?
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vishvonmeShadashAyAM deshikanAthasya yAvAnprasaraH | kalalAvasthayAM (sthito.api) vishvanimeShe.api tAvAnbhavati
close_translation: In the state of the world's opening, whatever the teacher-lord's outflow — even standing in the embryo-state, in the world's closing, he is as much.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: tripuTImayaM khalu samastaM tatra cha j~neye j~nAtari cha samam | dR^iDhagranthirj~nAnakalA kalayati trailokyamekakalam
close_translation: All [this] is indeed made of the triad — there, in the known and the knower, alike: the firmly-knotted knowledge-kalā makes the three worlds single-kalā.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kaH sadbhAvavisheShaH kusumAdbhavati gaganakusumasya | yatsphuraNAnuprANo lokaH sphuraNaM cha sarvasAmAnyam
close_translation: What real distinction arises of the sky-flower from the [real] flower? — that by whose flashing the world is quickened: and the flashing is common to all.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mANikyamaratakayoriva bhAvAbhAvayorbhedapratibhAsam | ekaraso.anyonya dvayorapyunmArShTi (dvayoH pramArShTi) sphuraNasambhedaH
close_translation: Like the ruby and the emerald: the appearance of the distinction of being-and-non-being — the one-taste, mutually, of the two, the flashing's distinction sweeps away (unmārṣṭi).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: aNDamaye nijapiNDapIThe sphuranti karaNadevyaH | prasphurati cha paramashivo j~nAnanidhishcha tAsAM madhye
close_translation: In the egg-made [universe], in one's own body-seat, the instrument-goddesses flash; and the supreme-Śiva flashes, the knowledge-treasure, in the midst of them.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sa tatrArchanIyo vimarshapuShpAdhivAsasurabhibhiH | chittachaShakArpitairvedyasudhAvIrapAnavastubhiH
close_translation: He is there to be worshipped with the fragrance of the reflexion-flowers' perfume, with the oblations of the experienced-nectar-drink offered in the cup of the mind.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: shrIpIThapa~nchavAho netratrayavR^indachakrANi smarata | smarata cha gurUNAM pa~Nkti pa~ncha cha shaktIH sR^iShTipramukhAH
close_translation: Remember the blessed seat's five currents (pañcavāha), the wheels of the three-eye-hosts; remember the gurus' row and the five powers headed by creation (sṛṣṭi).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: pIThe kalA nava pa~nchaiva pa~nchavAhapadavyAm | saptadasha phA(bhA)lanetre dvAdasha ShoDasha chAnyanetrayoH
close_translation: In the seat: the nine kalās and the five in the five-currents' path; the seventeen in the phāla-eye, the twelve and the sixteen in the other two eyes.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: prakaTitapa~nchaskandhe chatuShShaShTirbhavanti vR^indachakre | na khalu maNDale gurUNAM niyamo niyamAtila~NghinA (niyamAnalaM vinA) yuktaH
close_translation: In the revealed five-branched [tree], in the host-wheel, the sixty-four come to be; in the gurus' maṇḍala there is no rule, for the one who overpasses the rule [is not bound]. [variant: "without the rule's lack"]
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sR^iShTau dasha kalAH sthitau dvAvishatirbhavanti shaktayaH | ekAdasha saMhAre trayodasha tAsturIyaparvaNi
close_translation: In creation, the ten kalās; in maintenance, the twenty-two powers; the eleven in dissolution; the thirteen in the fourth-level.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: bhAsAyAM na vikalpAH sphurati sphuradekaniShkalashriyAm | yadi pratibimbagatyA sphurati paraM ShoDashAdhikA devI
close_translation: In the bhāsā (the illumination) there are no alternatives — she flashes in the flashing majesty of the single-partless; if by the reflection's way she flashes, the goddess is the sixteen-and-more (ṣoḍaśādhikā).
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sR^iShTeH pa~nchamakalA bhAseti jano gaNayati vyavadhAnam | sR^iShTermUlaskandhe bhAsAyAM pallavaH sR^iShTiH
close_translation: The fifth kalā of creation is called the bhāsā — people count [it] the interval. In the bhāsā, the root-branch of creation, the sprout [is] creation.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: nijabalanibhAlanameva varivasyA sA cha durlabhA loke | sulabhAni vishvapaterAsavatAmbUlagandhapuShpANi
close_translation: The service is the mere tending of one's own power — and that is rare in the world; easy [are] the world-lord's wine, betel, incense, and flowers.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vimraShTuM nijasattvaM vibhave kAryonmukhe stimite.api | bAhyavR^ittAntAnAM bha~NgaH prANasya saMyamo j~neyaH
close_translation: To reflect on one's own being, in the majesty, even [when] intent on the work and stilled: the breaking of the external activities — that is to be known as the prāṇa's restraint.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: shoSho malas.nAsho dAha etasya vAsanochChedaH | AplAvanaM tanUnAM j~nAnasudhAsekanirmitA shuddhiH
close_translation: The drying of the stain, the destruction, the burning of this, the cutting of the impression: the bathing of the bodies, made by the sprinkling of the knowledge-nectar — the purification.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: avikalpatayA vimarsho vikalpavargasyA~NgasannAhaH | arghyaM vedyavilAsaH puShpANi svabhAvapoShakAH bhAvAH
close_translation: The reflexion [is] by the non-alternative; the armor of the alternative-classes; the arghya [is] the known's display; the flowers [are] the states that nourish the own-nature.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: pUrNAhantAyA mukhe vishvavikalpA~NkurANAM vikShepam | mantrollekhavishuddhaM puNyaM kulabindutarpaNaM bhaNAmaH
close_translation: In the mouth of the full-I-ness, the scattering of the world's alternative-seeds: we declare the mantra-tracing's pure merit, the kula-bindu's libation.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yo yasya bhAvayogastasya khalu sa eva devatA bhavati | tadbhAvabhAvitA abhilaShita tathA phalanti pratimAH
close_translation: Whoever's state-union is his — he indeed becomes his deity; the images, made of that state, thus bear the desired [fruits].
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: chitraM na likhati chitraM chitrakaraH pashyata likhati tachchitram | tad bhaNata kutra yogyA kartuM dvayorapi (riti) devatAbuddhiH
close_translation: "The painting does not paint the painting; the painter paints — see, he paints that painting." Tell [us] where the deity-intelligence is fit to make, of the two.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: mananamayI nijavibhave nijasa~Nkochabhaye trANamayI | kavalitavishvavikalpA anubhUtiH kApi mantrashabdArthaH
close_translation: Made of thought in one's own majesty, made of protection in the fear of one's own shrinking; having devoured the world's alternatives — some such experience [is] the mantra-word's meaning.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: vaikhari(kA) nāma kriyA j~nAnamayI bhavati madhyamA vAk | ichChA punaH pashyantI sUkShmA sarvAsA samarasA vR^ittiH
close_translation: The vaikharī is the action; the madhyamā-speech is made of knowledge; the will again [is] the paśyantī — the subtle, the equal-taste's activity of all [the levels].
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: AnandollAsashrIH kShullakitAShTamahAsiddhisaubhAgyA | dR^ishyate yatra dashAyAM saiva devasya sarva(mahA)mudrAH
close_translation: The bliss-upsurge's fortune, adorned with the eight great-siddhis' good-luck — in whatever state she is seen, that [is] the god's all-(great-)mudrās.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: hR^idayasthAnaprarUDho vimarshakalpadrumo mahAshAkhaH | puShpyati bhogashriyA phalati cha niShkalasukhotsavAlokam
close_translation: Grown in the heart's place, the reflexion-wish-tree, the great-branched: it flowers with the enjoyment-fortune and fruits with the sight of the partless-bliss's festival.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kramiko bhavati na devastasya kathaM kAlakalmaShasparshaH | nityanirAvaraNasyApi (ko jIvato mokShapratyUhaH) ko.api jIvanmuktipratyUhaH
close_translation: The god is not sequential (kramika) — how [could there be] for him the touch of time's stain, [who is] ever-uncovered? What obstacle to the living one's liberation [could there be]?
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yat kimapi yena kenApi rUpeNa yatra kutrApi kiM nAsti | tasmAdAtmA nityasthiraH kShaNabha~Nga evAsthiro bhavati
close_translation: Whatever [is], in whatever form, wherever — nothing is not. Therefore the self is ever-stable; the momentary-breaking alone is unstable.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: nanvAtmanaH priyArthaM sarvasya priyatvaM bhaNati shrutiH | tasmAdAnandasvabhAva AtmA mukto.amukto vA
close_translation: "For the self's sake all is dear" — the śruti says. Therefore the self is of the bliss-nature, freed or unfreed.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yadi nijahR^idayollAsaM nirNetuM nityaniShkalamichChA | madhyatuTistruTitavyA asta~NgatayoH somasUryayosttarhi
close_translation: If the desire [is] to draw out one's own heart's upsurge, the ever-partless — then the middle's crack is to be broken, at the setting of the moon and the sun. [variant: "the middle's crack is to be broken, the weapon, of the moon and sun"]
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: sthUlatareShvapi prekShadhvaM bhUteShu khasya niShkalAvasthAm | ShaTtriMshikAtila~NghI kIdR^isho bhavatu somanAthaH
close_translation: Even in the grosser elements, look at the sky's partless-state: crossing the thirty-sixth, what should Somanātha be?
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ye kulakumbhasudhAsavapAnamahAmakhotsave pravartante | te khalu vikalpA~NkurasikA upadaShTuM pragalbhante
close_translation: Those who set out in the great sacrifice-festival of the kula-jar's nectar-wine-drinking — they, indeed, the tasters of the alternative-seeds, are bold to instruct.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: hanta mukhaM pratibimbatu pratibimbayatu tathA tadapi darpaNaH | darpaNaH punaryasmin pratibimbati so.api j~nAtavyaH
close_translation: "Ah — let the face be reflected; let the mirror also reflect that." And the mirror in which it is reflected — that too is to be known.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: avikArobhayapArshve chAShapi~njasadR^ikShe.arthe | antarmukho yogI bahirmukha iti kalpanA kutaH
close_translation: Unchanging on both sides, in the object like the ash-piñja's glance: "the yogi is inner-facing, outer-facing" — whence this imagining?
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yogI jAgarasvapnasuShuptyavasthAtrayasya paripATim | chitrAmiva maNimAlAM vimarshasUtraikagumphitAmudvahati
close_translation: The yogi bears the sequence of the three states — waking, dream, deep-sleep — like a pictured pearl-garland, threaded on the single reflexion-thread.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: ullokAnandasudhAshIdhurasodvejitena hR^idayena | abhilaShati lokayAtrAM tintiNicharvaNarasAntaraM yogI
close_translation: With the heart stirred by the surge of the upward-glance's bliss-nectar, the yogi longs for the world-course — [like one who] tastes the inner savor of the tintiṇī-chewing.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yAbhirgR^ihNAti yogI karaNapraNAlIbhirviShayasaukhyAni | nijahR^idayodvamanashIlAbhiH sphuraNamaya tAbhiH karoti trailokyam
close_translation: With the instrument-channels by which the yogi grasps the objects' joys — with those, whose nature is the heart's vomiting-out, he makes the three worlds flashing.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: yathA tava sthitistathAssva nishchinta iti pratiShThito.arthaH | tatrApyasti viveka evamupadishati ta(ka)sya ko.anyaH
close_translation: "As is your state, so be — unconcerned" — the established meaning. And in that too there is the discernment — thus he teaches; who else [could]?
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: aho saMsArasukhakelI aho sulabhaM mokShamArge saubhAgyam | truTitAta~Nkakala~NkA aho shivayoginAM yAmalI siddhiH
close_translation: Ah, the sport of saṃsāra's joy! Ah, the easy good-luck on the mokṣa-path! Ah, the yāmala-siddhi of the Śiva-yogis, its anxiety's stain broken!
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: kShaNamAtraspR^iShTenApyamR^itasvabhAvena j~nAnabhAvena | sarvottirNaH sarvaH sarvachiraM labhate sarvasaubhAgyam
close_translation: Touched for but a moment by the nectar-natured knowledge-state, the one who has crossed all obtains all, for long, all good-luck.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: gUDhAdguDhataro yo bhavati sphuTAdapi sphuTatara eShaH | daishikakaTAkShapAte pakShaH prathamo na bhavati dhanyAnAm
close_translation: He who is more hidden than the hidden, this one more manifest than the manifest: in the teacher's glance's fall, the first wing [is] not [given] to the fortunate.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: AstAmanyA vidyAshchatuHsrotasAmapi sAgarANAmiva | enamevAmR^itamayaM mathnAti manthAnabhairavo devaH
close_translation: Let the other vidyās be — like the seas of the four streams: this nectar-made one alone the Manthānabhairava-god churns.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: hanta rahasyaM bhaNAmo muDhA mA bhramata garbhagoleShu | atyAsanna hR^idaya paryAlochayata tasyodyogam
close_translation: "Ah, we tell the secret — O fools, do not wander in the wombs' globes: the heart is very near — consider its effort."
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)

sanskrit: enameva mahArthaM yuddhArambhe pANDuputrasya | ShoDashasahasrashaktirdeva upadishati sma mAdhavaH
close_translation: This very great-meaning, at the beginning of the Pāṇḍu-son's war, the god with the sixteen-thousand powers, Mādhava, taught. Thus — the one who unites the seventy mundane-sūtra-upsurges into one, descended from waking, that instant, the non-distinct dream; the answer to the promise; bound to the enterprise of the siddhi-path's going, fit to overleap the world; whose wealth is only the throat-bone and the skull — I praise that yoginī.
provenance: derived from our T1 (working translation, not peer reviewed)
